title: fix(cli): os validate, os build and os info count the objects an option-B project declares, so --strict stops refusing a conforming stack
body:
Fixes #17527

Clause-②: no

Re-derived from the delivered diff, not carried over from the claim: the diff adds no schema key, no closed-set member, no published export and no registry entry. `MetadataStats` is unchanged, `collectMetadataStats` was already exported, and no authorable key moves.

## The defect

`collectMetadataStats` (`packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts`) — the one reader behind the metadata summary that `os validate`, `os build`/`os compile` and `os info` all print — counted every collection at the **top level only**. On an ADR-0130 D4 / option-B project (every definition inside `packages[]`, none flattened up) all three reported a project that declares nothing, and `os validate` raised `No objects defined — this stack has no data model` on a stack that declares a data model.

Under `--strict` that warning is the gating error, so a **conforming project could not pass its own validator**, and the sentence it died on was false on its face.

## The fix

The fold goes **inside the reader**, not at the three call sites, for two reasons:

1. one seam answers for all three commands (`commands/validate.ts`, `commands/compile.ts`, `commands/info.ts`), and
2. `test/option-b-reader-acceptance.pin.test.ts` measures readers by **calling** them — a row can only attach to a callable, and that file explicitly forbids a row shaped like "assert `config.objects` is non-empty", because such a row is a second copy of the read it watches.

It reuses `authoringRuleUnionStack` (`utils/stack-collections.ts`), this package's single resolution rule for a package-owned collection. ⛔ No second fold was written. The seam's rule is strictly additive — a key the top level already carries **wins**, because in today's additive shape that array already *is* the union — which is exactly the property this reader needs.

## Acceptance

### 1. The card's repro, through the real binaries, before and after

`node packages/cli/bin/run.js`, built from this branch's tree in both directions. The stack is the card's own: no top-level `objects`, one clean `packages[]` entry.

**BEFORE** (`os validate --strict`, exit **1**):

```
  ✓ Validation passed (59ms)

  ob v1.0.0

  Data: 0 Objects
  UI: 0 Apps
  Logic: 0 Flows
  Security: 0 Positions  0 Permissions
  Runtime: 0 plugins

  ⚠ No objects defined — this stack has no data model
  ⚠ No apps or plugins defined — this stack may not do much

  ✗ Strict mode: warnings treated as errors
```

**AFTER** (same command, same stack):

```
  ✓ Validation passed (72ms)

  ob v1.0.0

  Data: 1 Objects  2 Fields
  UI: 0 Apps
  Logic: 0 Flows
  Security: 0 Positions  0 Permissions
  Runtime: 0 plugins

  ⚠ No apps or plugins defined — this stack may not do much

  ✗ Strict mode: warnings treated as errors
```

The false `No objects defined` line is gone and the count is right. ⚠️ **This stack still exits 1, and that is correct** — the card's minimal repro declares no apps and no plugins, so the *second* warning is true of it. `--strict` gates on the warning **list**, so "exit 1 to exit 0" needs a stack with nothing left to warn about. Stated rather than papered over, because the acceptance asked for the exit flip and the minimal repro cannot produce it.

The same option-B project with an app and a view — still entirely inside `packages[]`, nothing at the top level — goes **exit 1 to exit 0**:

```
  ✓ Validation passed (82ms)

  ob v1.0.0

  Data: 1 Objects  2 Fields
  UI: 1 Apps  1 Views
  Logic: 0 Flows
  Security: 0 Positions  0 Permissions
  Runtime: 0 plugins
```

`exit=0`, no warnings at all. That is the deliverable triage asked for: a legal project passing its own validator.

### 2. All three call sites

Same stack, same binary, after the fix — `os validate`, `os build` and `os info` each print `Data: 1 Objects  2 Fields`. Before the fix all three printed `Data: 0 Objects`. Full byte captures in the report.

### 3. The double-count control — union, not sum

Driven through the built reader, four shapes:

| stack | objects reported |
|:--|:--|
| top level only, one object | **1** |
| `packages[]` only, the same object | **1** |
| **BOTH** — the object at the top level AND inside `packages[]` | **1** — the union |
| two **distinct** packages, one object each | **2** — positive control |

The third row is the hazard and it answers 1. The fourth row is why that 1 is a measurement: without it, `toBe(1)` would also be satisfied by a fold that silently stopped reading `packages[]`.

The second named hazard — *the same package reached twice* — cannot double-count either, and the reason is stronger than "it counts once": `resolveArtifactPackageOrder` is the gate on artifact package identity and it **refuses** the artifact.

```
  ✗ Release artifact declares package "com.example.ob" more than once (`packages[1]` repeats an
    earlier entry). One artifact carries each package once — an artifact is one atomic delivery
    (ADR-0130 D1/D6), not a list with last-writer-wins.
```

ADR-0112 envelope, `code: DUPLICATE_ARTIFACT_PACKAGE`, `status: 422`, pinned in the new unit test by code **and** status (a bare `toThrow()` would stay green against an unnamed `Error`).

### 4. The top-level-only control — byte-identical

`os info` on the top-level stack is byte-identical before and after, `diff` clean. `os validate --strict` and `os build` differ in exactly the two wall-clock lines they print (`Load time: 21ms` / `28ms`, `✓ Validation passed (55ms)` / `(66ms)`) and in nothing else — those two lines vary between consecutive runs of the *same* binary, so they are not a reading about this change. Every printed count, warning and exit code is unchanged.

That is not a coincidence of the fixture: `authoringRuleUnionStack` returns a stack whose top level carries its collections **by identity**, so for every stack the platform emits today this reader's answer cannot move.

### 5. Ablation — the fold mutated back, both legs symmetric

Run from the **committed** state, so both legs have a restore point that really exists.

**Mutate leg.** `const stack: any = authoringRuleUnionStack(config);` replaced by a marked identity read:

```
anchor count before  'authoringRuleUnionStack(config)' : 1
marker count before  'OS_ABLATION_17527'               : 0
--- ON-DISK PROOF (mutation) ---
anchor count after   'authoringRuleUnionStack(config)' : 0
marker count after   'OS_ABLATION_17527'               : 2
post-mutation hash   = ab787a24f4def0c64cc2c69a3a6d3db2eab10c68   (HEAD blob 780c6cd1…)
```

Rebuilt, then proven to have reached the built artifact before the run's colour was allowed to mean anything:

```
✓ dist/: marker present in 1 built file -- the ablation is live in the artifact the suite consumes.
  hit  packages/cli/dist/utils/format.js
```

The run, ablated:

```
 FAIL  test/option-b-reader-acceptance.pin.test.ts > THE PIN — the subsystems that lose their
       collections under option B are EXACTLY the ledgered ones
  LOST     B2/B3 · cli metadata summary (collectMetadataStats — validate, build, info) ·
           every counted collection = 0

 FAIL  src/utils/format.metadata-stats-package-fold.test.ts
        > the card's repro: an option-B stack reports its objects and fields instead of zero
        > the fold reaches EVERY counted member, not just `objects`
        > POSITIVE CONTROL for the row above — two DISTINCT packages really do add up
        > the same package reached TWICE is REFUSED at the seam, so it cannot double-count

 Test Files  2 failed (2)
      Tests  5 failed | 11 passed (16)
```

⭐ **A discrimination, not a blanket red.** 4 of the 8 unit rows go red and 4 stay green — and the 4 that stay green are exactly the ones that must: the top-level-only row, the declares-nothing row, the union control (`toBe(1)` is *also* the unmutated answer), and the present-wins row. A mutation that reddened all 8 would have told me the fixture was carrying the assertion.

The same mutated binary is where this PR's BEFORE bytes come from, which is what makes them a measurement of this change rather than of a different tree.

**Restore leg**, symmetric and proven the same way:

```
✓ dist/: marker absent from all 508 built files -- the artifact the suite consumes no longer carries it.
✓ tree: working tree clean against HEAD -- nothing of this ablation is recorded outside dist/.
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
```

Restore verified by hash identity against the HEAD blob (`780c6cd1…` both sides) and a **whole-tree** `git status --porcelain`, not a per-path diff.

**The probe's row-count floor was measured at the boundary too**, the way the file's own comment demands. Written `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(37)`:

```
AssertionError: The probe measured 36 rows … expected 36 to be greater than or equal to 37
```

So 36 is the exact count with no slack, and the floor cannot be satisfied by construction.

## Behaviour change worth calling out

The fold resolves package order through `resolveArtifactPackageOrder`, whose ADR-0112 refusals are deliberately not swallowed. `os validate` and `os compile` already drive that seam on the same config **above** their summary call, so their behaviour on a malformed `packages` is unchanged — measured. `os info` did not, so it now reports a duplicate-package stack as a named `422` through its own `catch` instead of printing `Data: 0 Objects` for an artifact it could not read. That is the "absence must be loud" direction, and it is in the changeset.

## Acceptance notes

One finding, filed rather than folded in:

- `os info` prints its `Objects:` / `Apps:` / `Agents:` **detail** lists, and its `--json` `objects: []` array, from `config.objects` / `config.apps` / `config.agents` directly. Those are separate top-level-only reads from the summary this card names, and the presentation question they raise (per-package grouping vs a flat list) is not one this card decided. After this fix `os info` on an option-B stack prints `Data: 1 Objects` with no `Objects:` section under it — a visible residue, and the same shape of finding as this card was to #17069. **Filed as #17790** rather than widened into this PR — `os info --json` reports `stats.objects: 1` and `objects: []` in the same payload on such a stack, and whether the detail listing should be a flat union or grouped per package is a published-output-shape decision nobody has made.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived **62** families from the delivered five-path change set; all 62 ran, and reconciliation with recorded exit codes reports:

```
Run reconciliation — 62 derived, 62 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 62 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 62 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED
  (a DERIVED zero — all 62 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3).
```

Two of them first answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` / exit **3** — `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage`, both of which read built output — and are recorded green only after a full `turbo run build`, never as a passing 3. Re-derived after fetching a newer `origin/main`: the family set came back identical, 0 added and 0 removed.

Beyond the derived set:

- `pnpm lint` — the lane's standing addition, run **unnarrowed** (`eslint . --no-inline-config` over the whole repo), exit 0 in 82s. No scoping claim to defend.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit` — **198 files, 2829 tests, all passing**. The `integration` tier is declared to CI: the delivered diff touches no integration-tier file, no spawn entry point and no driver/kernel boot path, and `test/option-b-reader-acceptance.pin.test.ts` is classified `unit` by `vitest-tiers.ts` (measured — the integration population is 45 files and carries no `option-b` entry).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` — exit 0, including `check:test-typecheck` over the test layer.
- `scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 17775` — exit **0**: *"the clause-② declaration is readable in the fixed spelling and both carriers agree, and its diff carries no widening tell."*

Heavy verification went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` throughout; every verdict quoted above is the wrapper's own `VERDICT command-exit` line.
